1421091:
Lab 01 — DRIVER Target Selection

Category: Tuesday authenticated completion checkout, 25 or 0.

Mission

Learn DRIVER by completing one small, honest cycle: define a research-selection decision, represent a transparent screen, implement it with or without live data, validate one load-bearing claim, evolve the policy once, and reflect on a provisional public-company target. Technology readiness is the opening gate; the graded work is the finance workflow and decision.

Training sequence

  1. Readiness gate. Download Preflight Check and run the downloaded preflight_check.py locally or in Colab. If the primary path fails, preserve the exact symptom and download Offline Screening Case; use the downloaded offline-screening-case.csv. Name the owner and next action; never fabricate a successful download.
  2. Define & Discover — AI off. State the decision user, public-operating-company universe, exclusions, two measurable criteria, and one overriding disqualifier. Exclude banks, insurers, REITs, funds, shells, and other non-operating vehicles because the later Project 1 architecture is FCFF/enterprise-value based.
  3. Represent — human first. Write definitions, periods, thresholds or weights, missing-data treatment, and the smallest output needed to compare candidates.
  4. Implement the decision, not code — AI enabled. Use the published Week 1 dual-system packet, or send the same policy to two accessible course-supported systems. Author one follow-up probe and use a free interface when available; otherwise place COURSE-RUN PROBE: plus the exact probe and prediction in the AI-use checkout field. Mark one material suggestion accept, modify, reject, or unresolved, then apply your own policy to the live instructor diagnostics or the named offline case. Code implementation begins in Lab 02. No purchase is required and the access route never changes the scoring standard.
  5. Validate — AI may test; the human decides. AI may propose a test, but you independently check one load-bearing definition or company fact against provider documentation, a filing, or another authoritative source and decide whether the evidence is acceptable.
  6. Evolve — human-run in Lab 01; AI-assisted options begin in Lab 02. Test one alternative threshold, definition, or exclusion. Retain or revise the policy based on the result; do not manufacture a change.
  7. Reflect — human-owned. State what you now know, what remains unknown, and the observable evidence that would change your mind. Then select one provisional target for deeper valuation research.

This first cycle is a deliberate human-baseline calibration, so the middle is not yet fully AI-forward. Lab 02 is the first complete AI-accelerated middle: AI supports implementation, failure-hypothesis generation, and an Evolve robustness option; the student still owns the Define/Discover boundary, independent acceptance, and final Reflect decision.

The screen selects a research target. It does not establish a buy recommendation or intrinsic value. Asbury Automotive Group (ABG) is the instructor demonstration and is ineligible. Banks, insurers, REITs, funds, shells, and other non-operating vehicles are also ineligible for this Project 1 path.

Individual Brightspace checkout fields

  1. Lab Date (mm/dd/yyyy).
  2. Teammates and personal contribution (Purdue usernames; enter worked individually when applicable, then state what you personally defined, ran, checked, and decided).
  3. Readiness evidence: working path or exact blocker, fallback used, next action, and owner.
  4. Problem and decision: decision user, universe, research-selection purpose, and exclusions.
  5. Human baseline: two criteria with definitions and thresholds/weights plus one overriding disqualifier, written before generative AI.
  6. AI-use record: named access path; exact student-authored follow-up probe and prior prediction; returned or pending staff return status; and one material suggestion accepted, modified, rejected, or unresolved.
  7. Decision evidence: live source/provider and period/as-of date, or exact offline-case label; concise candidate comparison and provisional company/ticker.
  8. Validate, evolve, reflect: independent source/date/finding; alternative tested; retained or revised policy; what is known/unknown; and observable disqualifier/change condition.
  9. Optional artifact link if a durable repository/notebook exists.
  10. Truth and in-person attendance attestation: “I attended this session in person and completed this checkout only for myself. I produced and checked the evidence above, disclosed my AI use, and did not expose credentials.”
  11. Receipt confirmation: submit and open the Brightspace attempt/receipt before leaving.

Completion standard

Full credit requires an on-time authenticated attempt that directly answers every field, contains the requested personal work record, ends in a provisional target (or a defensible no admissible target yet result), and includes the attestation. Completing apply_student_screen() is not required until Lab 02. A reproducible technical failure can satisfy readiness evidence when the fallback finance task is completed; technology failure does not excuse or invalidate the finance decision work.
1421099:
Lab 02 — Screen Validation and Research Admission

Category: Thursday merit checkout, 0–25.

Mission

Act as an equity-research gatekeeper. Decide whether the provisional Lab 01 company should be admitted, replaced, or held for more evidence before valuation work. A composite score is not evidence by itself; the policy, definitions, data, robustness, and judgment must agree.

Training sequence

1. Reconstruct the workflow — AI off

Map each DRIVER stage to one artifact from Lab 01. Repair any missing decision boundary, definition, exclusion, or missing-data rule before asking AI for help.

2. Hostile peer review

Have teammates attack one criterion, one exclusion, and the overriding disqualifier. Record each challenge and mark it accept, modify, or reject with evidence.

3. AI-enabled failure search

Download Screening Starter and implement your transparent rule in the downloaded screening_starter.py. Use the published Week 1 dual-system packet, two accessible course-supported systems, or the returned private course-run probe. Ask for distinct plausible ways the screen could select the wrong research target. Preserve the hypotheses; do not accept either as fact until tested. A late staff-returned probe is recorded as pending and cannot reduce the score; use the packet while the access issue is cured.

4. Validate and Evolve — AI may accelerate; the human decides

  • verify one load-bearing label, period, adjustment, or company fact against an authoritative source dated as of the analysis;
  • change one defensible threshold, weight, lookback, or exclusion and compare ranks;
  • test one missing-data or provider-disagreement treatment; and
  • explain which result is economically material rather than merely numerically different.

AI may propose or implement the changed-input/missingness test during Evolve, but you must state the expected direction first, inspect the result, and decide whether to retain, revise, or reject the change. Independent source acceptance and the final decision remain human-owned.

5. Research-admission decision

Deliver a 45-second oral defense to a peer or TA: target, two dated facts, most sensitive assumption, remaining unknown, admission decision, and observable reversal trigger. Record the synthesized decision in the checkout. Replace and hold for more evidence are strong outcomes when the analysis supports them.

Individual Brightspace checkout fields

  1. Lab Date (mm/dd/yyyy).
  2. Teammates and personal contribution.
  3. Problem and decision: decision user, universe, and admission standard.
  4. Reconstructed DRIVER evidence map: stage → artifact/result.
  5. Peer red-team dispositions: criterion, exclusion, and disqualifier challenges with accept/modify/reject decisions.
  6. AI-use record: named access path and only model identifiers actually exposed; distinct failure hypotheses; one accepted, modified, or rejected implementation suggestion and why.
  7. Data and evidence: source, returned period/as-of date, definitions, and ranked output.
  8. Independent validation: claim checked, authoritative source/date, and conclusion.
  9. Robustness evidence: changed input, original/revised ranks, missing-data/provider test, and economic interpretation.
  10. Decision/action: admit, replace, or hold; company/ticker; material unknown; and an observable disqualifier or reversal trigger.
  11. Optional artifact link when a durable artifact exists.
  12. Truth and in-person attendance attestation: confirm you attended this session in person and the work and AI-use record are your own and accurate.
  13. Receipt confirmation: submit and open the Brightspace attempt/receipt.

Merit anchors — 5 points each

For any criterion, use these intermediate anchors: 4 = sound with one minor, non-load-bearing weakness; 2 = relevant evidence but an important link is incomplete; 1 = minimal relevant attempt; 0 = missing, inaccessible, nonresponsive, or fabricated.

Merit anchors — 5 points each
Criterion 5 — strong observable evidence 3 — usable but incomplete 0–1 — not demonstrated
Problem and decision specific user, universe, admission standard, exclusions, and success test usable decision with one vague boundary generic “best stock” or no research gate
Data and evidence integrity dated sources, periods, definitions, exclusions, missing-data treatment, and output are traceable output exists with one minor traceability gap untraceable ranking, mixed definitions, or wrong object
Validation and robustness independent source check, genuine changed-input test, and missing/provider attack are interpreted checks exist but one is mechanical or weakly interpreted AI agreement treated as validation or no falsification attempt
Financial judgment admit/replace/hold follows the evidence and includes uncertainty plus an observable trigger defensible target with a vague condition unsupported buy claim or score treated as truth
Explanation and transfer causal defense, DRIVER-to-artifact ownership, and AI dispositions are clear; method transfers understandable but mostly descriptive copied output, framework recitation, or no ownership evidence

Do not award points for confidence, effort, speaking style, personality, or claimed growth. Score one underlying defect once under the most relevant criterion.
